records.section_heading: GOVERNMENT OF AMERICAN SAMOA 66799 OFFICE OF MARINE RESOURCES
records.question: What were the three objectives of the project described in the report?
records.ground_truth_answer: The objectives were: (1) to re-establish six aggregation devices in the waters around Tutuila Island; (2) to "beef up" the materials from which the FAD's were constructed, thereby giving them life expectancies of five to ten years; and (3) to reap the benefits accruing from the system.
ground_truth_chunks: Its objectives were 1) to re-establish six aggregation devices in the waters around Tutuila Island; 2) to "beef up" the materials from which the FAD's were constructed, thereby giving them life expectancies of five to ten years; and 3) to reap the benefits accruing from the system.

records.question: Which FAD had the longest lifespan and how long did it remain in position?
records.ground_truth_answer: FAD C<sub>3</sub> — it remained in position for over thirteen months and had the longest lifespan of any deployed by OMR to date.
ground_truth_chunks: FAD C<sub>3</sub>- Deployed in August, 1981 by the "SAUSAUIMOANA".
This FAD remained in position for over thirteen months and had the longest lifespan of any deployed by OMR to date.

records.question: According to the section, what was the major cause of FAD loss and what remedies were suggested?
records.ground_truth_answer: The major cause was the mooring line floating on or near the surface where it was cut by a boat keel or propellor; suggested remedies were elimination of slack or scope from the mooring, use of negatively buoyant line, or use of a counterweight to sink the line.
ground_truth_chunks: The major cause appears to be related to the mooring line floating on or near the surface where it was cut by a boat keel or propellor.
The problem could be solved by the elimination of slack or scope from the mooring, the use of negatively buoyant line, or the use of a counterweight to sink the line.

records.question: According to Job III-1 monthly trolling surveys, what were the average catch rates (lbs/hr) near FADs B and C compared to elsewhere?
records.ground_truth_answer: Average catch rate near FADs B and C was 28.2 lbs/hr versus 15.7 lbs/hr elsewhere (almost twice as great near FADs).
ground_truth_chunks:
A total of 13.25 hours of survey effort has been expended around FAD's B and C since 1981 and 125.75 hours have been expended elsewhere. A total of 374 lbs of fish were caught near the FAD's for an average catch of 28.2 lbs/hr. A total of 1977 lbs were caught elsewhere for an average of 15.7 lbs/hr. Catch rate in the vicinity of FAD's was, thus, almost twice as great as in other areas. The FAD

catches were dominated by blue marlin, yellowfin and dolphin.
